conflict_topics: closing bedroom doors to block smell
weekday cooking rota and night assignments (swaps for late arrivals)
dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation is concise and cooperative; proposals are concrete (who washes, extractor/window, rota, swaps).
Agents give brief reasons tied to needs (Agent A: cooking is break/buys shared items; Agent B: needs to sleep early; Agent D: gets home late).
Little needless repetition; extractor/window and bedroom doors are mentioned multiple times but as legitimate conditions rather than filler.
All parties propose or accept concrete actions (wash pan now, pick nights), which supports quick agreement.
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive conflict arose in the transcript. The group agreed on a practical set of rules: 'whoever cooks washes their pans'; keep extractor and window on while cooking; close bedroom doors if the smell gets strong; implement a weekday rota with swaps for late arrivals. Assigned nights: Monday (Agent A), Tuesday (Agent B), Wednesday (Agent C), Friday (Agent D).
position_change_notes: Agent A initially proposed either 'whoever cooks washes' or a rota, then accepted a weekday rota and took Monday—soft shift from alternative to rota.
Agent D proposed the rota (raising fairness for late arrivals) and then accepted taking Friday with the option to swap.
Agent B added ventilation/door conditions early and ultimately accepted the rota and took Tuesday.
Agent C accepted the washing rule and took Wednesday without changing position.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A proposes a rule and offers to wash the pan and use extractor/window. Agent B accepts the rule and adds a request to keep extractor/window on and shut bedroom/corridor doors if smell gets strong ('Please keep the extractor and window on while you cook, and shut bedroom/corridor doors if the smell gets strong'). No incompatible demands were expressed.

Agent A repeats commitment to wash the pan and use extractor/window and says they will ask C and D to agree. Agent B repeats the request and asks C and D to agree. This is coordination, not disagreement.

Agent C agrees to 'whoever cooks washes their pans.' Agent D agrees to wash and use extractor/window but proposes a weekday rota for fairness ('can we do a simple weekday rota...'). The rota proposal is a new proposal, not an expressed conflict.

Agent A accepts the rota suggestion and proposes assigning weekday cooking nights. Agent B agrees to the rota with the previously stated conditions and asks to pick nights now. No incompatible positions remain.
Agent C picks Wednesday. Agent D picks Friday and offers to swap if they get home late. Participants continue assigning nights without disagreement.

Agent A takes Monday; Agent B takes Tuesday and accepts swapping if late. All four weekday slots are assigned and the group has agreed on rules (whoever cooks washes pans; use extractor/window; close bedroom doors if smell strong; swaps allowed). No substantive conflict remains.

substantive_insights: Main practical tensions were smell spread and unwashed shared cookware; solutions combined ventilation, personal washing responsibility, and scheduling.
Fairness concerns (late arrivals) were addressed by allowing swaps and making a rota, which resolved potential distributional disputes preemptively.
Agreement centered on concrete, enforceable behaviors (who washes, when to run extractor, closing doors, assigned nights), which reduced room for ambiguity.
